findings.claim: The first decision's log line in every new repository says it was added `with kmctl new decision`, but kmctl init wrote it, so the log misstates the actor.

When init writes the first decision into a kept bundle it appends to the kept .okf/log.md and .okf/decisions/index.md (and .okf/index.md when the section is new), yet prints `kept .okf/log.md (already there)` and lists neither file under `updated` in --json, so the output says a changed file was left alone.
The broken-marker warning always says the file has kmctl:start without a kmctl:end after it, which is wrong for a file with only an end marker or with two start markers.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan says.

Init writes the four rules, adds one block per real agent file (symlink-aware), records the first decision only when no record has its title, prints the next steps last, and a second run changes nothing.
Gates and every eval row pass on my own stamp.
Spike 2 settles r7.
Three small, non-blocking findings: a log line names the wrong command, the output says "kept" for files init appended to, and one warning's wording is off.
None of them needs another review.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests and eval rows r1-r6 and r8 all pass; "stamp green: a452a395575921ee8ce2793af824b42c623a9315f685fe7cd8bc272365f6febb".

I ran `kmctl init` from the worktree in scratch repos and read what it wrote: fresh repo: 11 files, `kmctl check` passes; the decision has Context, Decision with three rejected alternatives, and Consequences, plus its index entry and log line; repo with an existing CLAUDE.md: text kept, block appended once; CLAUDE.md symlinked to AGENTS.md: the link stays and AGENTS.md gets one block; AGENTS.md only: block added, no CLAUDE.md created, as the plan says; existing block: only the block is replaced, the text around it is kept, and a re-run reports kept; bundle with decisions 0001-0003: init writes 0004, check passes, a re-run writes nothing; record with the title already at 0001: nothing written; start marker without an end marker, and non-UTF-8 AGENTS.md: the file is left alone and init warns; init run twice: `diff -r` shows no change.
The four packaged rule files: no mention of loopctl, tickets or `.loop/`; each has `paths:` front matter and WHY paragraphs, in plain language.
The diagrams rule tells the reader to adjust its `paths:` to their own layout.
The 43-of-53 count in okf-bundle is framed as coming from the source repository, which is honest.
Eval tests: r1-r5 and r8 each assert their fails_when.
r2's symlink test asserts exactly one block through `_block`'s count.
r5 snapshots every file's bytes and mtime.
r3 covers a fresh repo, a repeat run on this repo's bundle, and a title already at 0003.
Other test edits: test_new_concept, test_supersede and test_adr_audit_fixes only renumber, and the supersede refusal cases keep the same meaning.
The test_briefing state test verifies init's decision, so "1 concept due" still checks the singular form.
The new briefing test pins the routing, rules and skills against a plain bundle.
test_init_creates_no_empty_folders now allows the non-empty decisions/ folder and still catches empty ones.
The briefing source and src/kmctl/rules/ have no diff, and the briefing is 526 words.
Docs: the tutorial's pasted output for init and `new decision` matches my real runs.
The reference page, how-to, explanation, manifesto clause, overview diagram and table, ADR 0011, and the ADR 0002 Correction all agree with the code.
The init help and the ScaffoldResult docstring name both exceptions.

r7 (judgment): spike 2's stdout shows 5/5/4 decisions beyond 0001, each naming a rejected alternative, an architecture page in 3/3 runs, and check passing in 3/3, against spike 1's 3.00 with 0/3 and 4.33 with 3/3.
The row is met.

f1: `new_concept` writes "Added `decisions/0001-...` with `kmctl new decision`." into the log of a repo where the user only ran `kmctl init`, so the log names the wrong command (the builder flagged this too).
Rewriting that one log line after `new_concept`, or letting the writer take the verb name, fixes it.
f2: in a kept bundle, init appends to `.okf/log.md` and the decisions index, but the human output prints them under "kept ... (already there)" and `--json` has them only in `skipped`.
Help and docs do name this exception, but the per-file output contradicts them.
Listing those files under `updated`, or leaving them out of `kept`, would make the output true.
f3: `_with_block` returns None for three cases (end before start, a start marker with no end marker, two start markers), but the warning text describes only the second.
With `x\n<!-- kmctl:end -->\n` it says the file "has <!-- kmctl:start --> without one <!-- kmctl:end -->".
A dangling CLAUDE.md symlink makes init write the block to the link's target, creating that file, and report "created CLAUDE.md".
This is reasonable, but it could write outside the repo if the link points there.
With AGENTS.md only, Claude Code (which reads CLAUDE.md) does not see the block.
The plan chose this behavior, and the briefing still reaches Claude Code.
docs/tutorials/get-started-with-kmctl.md line 107 is an unwrapped long line.
